A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an LSTM framework which is capable of learning features from raw trajectory data in order to predict the future trajectory and detect abnormal events.
we present an end-to-end trainable model that can predict the future motion and detect abnormalities in a surveillance scene with no prior information about the environment or the people in it.

we present an LSTM framework for human trajectory prediction and abnormal event detection where we learn the features directly from the input data and use a combined attention model to capture the spatial and temporal context of the pedestrians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single model can be trained to perform two different tasks (trajectory prediction and abnormal event detection) by only changing the loss function.
by combining the power of attention mechanisms with recurrent architectures we can achieve state-of-the-art results on two different challenging tasks.
the proposed model can be applied in a variety of applications where the task requires modelling human motion.
